summary: This is the farmers' market app rewritten so that each stream pipeline does exactly one job well: one method collects every vendor name into a unique, alphabetically sorted list, and another builds a short menu for a single vendor that stops after three items.

lines.text: Collectors supplies the recipes that turn a finished stream back into a collection, and Collectors.toList() is the one used at the end of every method here.
All the stream methods below read from this one list, so the products you add here are the raw data for every report the program prints.
Even though the method name still says "Set," it now hands back a List, because a list is what can promise a stable alphabetical order.
Storing the vendor name in a variable means the same spelling is reused for the menu and for the discount calculation, so the two reports cannot drift apart.
forEach with a method reference prints each menu line on its own row, which reads better than dumping the whole list inside square brackets.
The null check on getSeason() comes before the call to toLowerCase(), which is what stops a product with no season recorded from crashing the pipeline.
Sorting happens while the elements are still MarketProduct objects, because once map has reduced them to names the price is no longer available to sort by.
map converts each product into just its name, changing the stream's element type from MarketProduct to String.
This drops missing and whitespace-only vendor names so that blank entries never reach the sorted output.
distinct removes duplicate vendor names, giving the uniqueness that a Set used to provide.
Called with no argument, sorted() uses the natural ordering of the elements, which for String means alphabetical.
equalsIgnoreCase matches the vendor even if the capitalization in the data differs from the name passed in, and both null checks guard the comparison.
This line is commented out on purpose: with a limit of three, sorting first would change which three products survive, so leave it off until you decide you want the alphabetically first three.
String.format with %.2f pins each price to two decimal places, so 3.5 prints as 3.50 like real money.
limit stops the stream once three elements have passed through, which is what keeps the printed menu short.
